2.  The present writ petition has been filed for the following reliefs :-
(a) for quashing of order dated 28.06.2023 (Annexure-4) passed by Additional Collector-cum- Rakesh Prasad vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153125555/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Arbitrator (respondent no. 4) whereby and whereunder the respondent no.4 has not considered the claim of the petitioners for payment of adequate/ fair compensation amount with regard to acquisition of their land for construction of NH-75 (SEC-V) on the basis of market value in terms of Section 26 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and awarded less/ meager amount of compensation than the market value,
(b) for issuance of an appropriate writ(s), order(s), direction(s) or a writ in the nature of mandamus commanding upon the respondents to pay the fair/ adequate compensation to the petitioners with regard to acquisition of their land for- construction of National Highway-75 (SEC-V), when other land loosers namely Rajendra Pratap Dev & others whose land (agricultural/ rural) situated at Narkhoria Kala Village/ Mouza-- Narkhoria Kala (adjacent/ near village) was also acquired for the same purpose has received highest rate i.e. Rs.2,76,080/- (Annexure- 6) for per decimal which is highest rate in comparison to another land looser including the petitioners.
3. After some arguments, learned counsel for the petitioners seeks permission with withdraw the present writ petition with a liberty to work out his remedy in accordance with law.
4. Learned counsels for the respondents have no objection.
6. Accordingly, the present writ petition is, hereby, disposed of with the aforesaid liberty.

7. Pending interlocutory application, if any, also stands disposed of.
(Rajesh Kumar, J.) Chandan/-
